config.intro: Configure the SFTP destination. The host process must have network access to the configured server.

config.field.server.label: Server
config.field.server.help: Hostname or IP of the SFTP server. The host process must have network access to it on the configured port.
config.field.port.label: Port
config.field.port.help: TCP port. SFTP runs over SSH; default 22. Change when the SSH daemon listens on a non-standard port.
config.field.auth_method.label: Authentication Method
config.field.auth_method.help: How the SSH client proves its identity to the server.
config.field.username.label: Username
config.field.username.help: SSH username. Required for every auth method.
config.field.password.label: Password
config.field.password.help: SSH password. Required for password auth. For keyboard-interactive, echoed back to password-style prompts; multi-factor prompts that need operator interaction return empty. Stored encrypted at rest via AES-256-GCM.
config.field.private_key_path.label: Private Key Path
config.field.private_key_path.help: PEM-encoded SSH private key. Required for publickey auth. The host process must be able to read it. Supports OpenSSH and RSA formats; PKCS#8 / PuTTY .ppk are not supported — convert with ssh-keygen -i.
config.field.private_key_passphrase.help: Optional passphrase for the private key. Leave blank for unencrypted keys.
config.field.agent_socket.label: SSH Agent Socket
config.field.agent_socket.help: Path to the SSH agent's UNIX socket. Required for agent auth. Windows named pipes are not supported in v1 — operators on Windows can run ssh-agent inside WSL or use ssh-agent -D plus a TCP-forwarded socket.
config.field.host_key_fingerprint.label: Host Key Fingerprint (SHA-256)
config.field.host_key_fingerprint.help: Optional. SHA-256 fingerprint of the server's host key (the form ssh-keygen -lf … -E sha256 emits). When set, the client verifies the server's key against this fingerprint and rejects mismatches (TOFU protection).
config.field.path.label: Subdirectory
config.field.path.help: Optional subdirectory on the SFTP server. Leave empty to write to the user's home directory. The plugin creates intermediate directories as needed (mkdir -p semantics).
config.field.connect_timeout.label: Connect Timeout
config.field.connect_timeout.help: Maximum time to wait for the SSH handshake. Minimum 5s. Use a longer value for high-latency networks.

guide.heading: SFTP storage destination setup
guide.intro: Configure the SFTP server, choose how the host authenticates, and verify with the Test connection button. The host process must have network access to the configured server and port.
guide.footer: Tip: enable host key fingerprint verification under "Host Key Fingerprint" to lock down the server identity. Get the fingerprint with: ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub -E sha256

guide.step.1.title: Verify network access
guide.step.1.body: From the host that runs McHarbor, confirm the SFTP server is reachable: nc -vz sftp.example.com 22
guide.step.2.title: Decide the authentication mode
guide.step.2.body: Pick how the host will prove its identity to the server. Password is the simplest; publickey is the most common in production; agent re-uses keys already loaded into ssh-agent; keyboard-interactive is for two-factor gateways (Duo, Okta, SecurID).
guide.step.3.title: Create or choose the SSH user
guide.step.3.body: On the SFTP server, create the user that will own the destination directory. Grant write access to the subdirectory configured below. Restrict the user's shell to SFTP-only with ForceCommand internal-sftp when possible.
guide.step.auth.password.title: Configure the password
guide.step.auth.password.body: Enter the SSH password for the user above. Stored encrypted at rest via AES-256-GCM. The host never logs the password.
guide.step.auth.publickey.title: Install the private key on the host
guide.step.auth.publickey.body: Copy the SSH private key to a path the host process can read (e.g. /etc/mcharbor/sftp_id_ed25519). Set the file mode to 0600 and the owner to the McHarbor process user. If the key is passphrase-protected, enter the passphrase below.
guide.step.auth.keyboard_interactive.bod: The host echoes the configured password back for password-style prompts. Multi-factor prompts that need operator interaction are returned empty — for full MFA automation, use the password auth method with a dedicated service account instead.
guide.step.auth.agent.title: Expose the SSH agent socket
guide.step.auth.agent.body: Start ssh-agent on the host (or in a sidecar container) and confirm the socket path (default /run/ssh-agent.sock). Add the destination user's identity to the agent with ssh-add. The host will pull signers from the agent at every connection.
guide.step.5.title: Test the connection
guide.step.5.body: Click "Test connection" on the storage location form. The host runs a four-step round-trip: connect / write a probe file / read it back / delete it. All four steps must succeed before the destination is considered healthy.
